turns.assessment: The event is a simultaneous, network-wide optical loss affecting many otherwise unrelated services and lightpaths, while the sole common working-path dependency is ROADM S20 (E1). The unchanged S14–S04 and S21–S10 line systems rule out the access portions of svc340, and a client-port or individual transceiver fault cannot explain the correlated OCH losses, protection switches, and adjacent OMS/OSC alarms. The best documented hard failure at the common ROADM is a WSS input-port failure.

proposals.rationale: ROADM S20 is the only element common to every affected working path. A failed WSS input port there can simultaneously block all channels entering on the affected degree, producing the broad OCH LOS and downstream client failures seen at t=602.5 s. Healthy monitored segments outside S20 and unaffected direct services exclude the svc340 endpoint ports and S21–S10 optical section.

clarify.assessment: The evidence does not identify which S20 ingress degree contains the alleged failed WSS port. Unchanged incoming channel monitors do not distinguish a downstream WSS port failure, while the explicit LOS/OSC alarms occur on both the S01 and S13 directions and therefore do not uniquely select one of the five candidates. Choosing a port would be speculative.

llm_alone.decision: commit not to one place (5 locations); reported as a set

score.why: truth not in the reported set
